primitives.name: Authentication Boundary
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Skill: Auth Boundary Use this when a website needs signed-in user state, login, logout, account-gated pages, profile loading, or protected file downloads.
primitives.assumptions: User identity is enforced through platform-managed session state and server-side validation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when client bypasses proxy or accesses internal endpoints directly.

layer2.mapping: The auth boundary maps browser requests to platform-verified identity proxies, maintaining consistent session semantics across UI and backend layers.
layer2.telemetry: Session token validity, unauthorized access attempts, and proxy response codes.

primitives.name: Platform Identity Contract
primitives.verbatim_quote: The platform owns auth and exposes a small contract to the website.
primitives.assumptions: Identity resolution is centralized and abstracted from client-side logic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when client assumes direct identity control or misuses platform endpoints.

layer2.mapping: The platform contract defines a minimal interface for identity operations, encapsulating all auth complexity within runtime.
layer2.telemetry: Endpoint access logs, identity injection success/failure rates, and SDK usage compliance.

primitives.name: Proxy Identity Resolver
primitives.verbatim_quote: This endpoint is the only user-profile endpoint browser components should fetch.
primitives.assumptions: Browser-facing identity is resolved through a controlled proxy to prevent exposure of internal auth details.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when raw internal endpoints are exposed or accessed without proxy mediation.

layer2.mapping: The proxy resolver ensures that browser identity queries map to secure internal identity sources without leaking sensitive headers or tokens.
layer2.telemetry: Request latency, cache hit ratio, and unauthorized header presence.

reasoning_traces.think:
The auth boundary enforces a strict separation between client-facing and platform-facing identity operations. Client-side code must route all identity-dependent requests through designated proxy endpoints, such as /api/user, which act as gatekeepers for fnf.internal/user. This design prevents direct access to internal auth mechanisms and avoids exposing sensitive headers or cookies to the UI. The platform injects identity on server egress, ensuring that auth state remains consistent and secure. The dual nature of auth—frontend identity proxy and backend SDK integration—requires careful handling of session state and endpoint routing. Failure modes include unauthorized access attempts, direct internal endpoint calls, or incorrect header propagation. These risks are mitigated by enforcing a contract where browsers only interact with app-local endpoints, and server code handles internal communication with automatic identity attachment.
